content.text:
Consumer Agents Signal New Phase for AI Growth: Goldman’s Eric Sheridan said its team estimated $1.4T in 2027 US hyperscaler capital deployment, above Wall Street consensus. He also cited constraints including memory chips, power, and land. This is a different stated measure from Bloomberg’s $1.2T AI-infrastructure-capex report. (time=2026-09-18; cutoff=BEFORE_CUTOFF).
Hyperscalers Need $300 Billion in Annual AI Revenue to Break Even: Goldman: The page reports $800B consensus 2026 capex, $1.1T 2027 consensus, and Goldman’s expectation that 2027 spending would beat consensus but with slower growth and smaller upside surprises. It also relays Goldman’s estimate of roughly $70B annualized cloud revenue above the pre-AI trend in Q2 and announced backlogs above $1.5T. (time=2026-09-25 08:11 (page display; timezone unspecified); cutoff=UNKNOWN).
Scoop: OpenAI’s Annual Recurring Revenue Nears $70B: Axios reported, citing people familiar with OpenAI’s financials, that its annualized revenue run rate was nearing $70B and business-to-business revenue had grown more than 100% since the start of Q3. Axios said it could not immediately determine OpenAI’s expenses. (time=2026-09-29T14:15:40Z; cutoff=BEFORE_CUTOFF).

content.text:
September 2026 Ramp AI Index: Cracks in the AI Thesis, Part 2: Ramp reported that business AI adoption was still growing but slowing; its sampled top-1% firms’ AI spend per employee fell 9.7% in August, and its token-price index was down 41% from its March peak. The author noted seasonal effects and sample volatility. (time=2026-09-09; cutoff=BEFORE_CUTOFF).
AI Adoption Is Spreading. AI Spending Is Concentrating: Apollo’s analysis of Ramp data said roughly 10% of software-spending businesses used a GPU vendor, up from under 4% two years earlier, while the top 10% of customers accounted for 99.5% of Ramp-sampled model-serving spend and 99% of neocloud spend. The figures describe the Ramp sample, not the whole AI market. (time=2026-09-24; cutoff=BEFORE_CUTOFF).
